dev.auth.decrypt_failed.note: Error reply when signing in or changing the password: the device could not decrypt the password the app sent (the apps encrypt it for each connection). Shown after "Error: " at sign-in.

dev.auth.device_state_failed.note: Error reply on the sign-in screen when the device could not tell whether it already has an owner password (a database problem on the device).

dev.auth.first_password_home_only.text: The owner password can only be chosen from your home network, at the device's own address and not through a proxy. You can also set it on the server: docker exec -i otc otc-entrypoint set-password, with the password as its input.
dev.auth.first_password_home_only.note: Error reply on the first-run screen of a device that runs in Docker (a container on a home server or NAS) when its first password is chosen from outside the home network, through the internet or through a proxy (a program that forwards the page from another address): for safety the device takes its first password only from the home network. The command after the colon is typed on the server the device runs on, with the password given as its input: keep it exactly as it is.

dev.auth.first_password_user_home_only.text: This account's first password can only be chosen from your home network, at the account's own address and not through a proxy, or at its address on the bridge.
dev.auth.first_password_user_home_only.note: Error reply on the first-run screen of an additional user's account (a user the owner added in Settings > Users) on a device that runs in Docker (a container on a home server or NAS), when the account's first password is chosen from outside the home network or through a proxy (a program that forwards the page from another address), and not through the bridge: for safety such an account takes its first password only from the home network, at its own address, or at its address on the bridge.

dev.auth.first_password_window_closed.text: The 30 minutes to choose the owner password here have passed. Set it on the server instead: docker exec -i otc otc-entrypoint set-password, with the password as its input.
dev.auth.first_password_window_closed.note: Error reply on the first-run screen of a device that runs in Docker (a container on a home server or NAS) when its first password is chosen more than 30 minutes after the device first started: for safety the device then takes it only on the server it runs on. The command after the colon is typed on that server, with the password given as its input: keep it exactly as it is.

dev.auth.invalid_session.note: Error reply when signing in with a password the device doesn't accept (a wrong password). Shown after "Error: ".

dev.auth.keypair_failed.note: Error reply on the sign-in screen when the device could not make the key the app encrypts the password with (one per connection).

dev.auth.no_public_key.text: no public key was requested for this connection
dev.auth.no_public_key.note: Error reply when signing in or changing the password on a connection where the app never asked the device for the key it encrypts the password with (an app fault). Shown after "Error: " at sign-in.

dev.auth.password_too_short.text: the password must have 8 characters or more
dev.auth.password_too_short.note: Error reply when choosing the device's first password, or a new one in Settings, that is shorter than 8 characters.

dev.auth.public_key_failed.note: Error reply on the sign-in screen when the device could not encode the key the app encrypts the password with (one per connection).

dev.auth.session_expired.text: Session expired or invalid, please sign in again.
dev.auth.session_expired.note: Error reply in the web app when its saved sign-in (kept for a while so the password isn't asked at every visit) has expired or is no longer valid: the user signs in with the password again.

dev.auth.token_failed.note: Error reply in the web app right after signing in when the device could not make the saved sign-in that spares typing the password at the next visit.

dev.auth.too_many_attempts.text: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds} seconds.
dev.auth.too_many_attempts.note: Error reply on the sign-in screen after too many wrong passwords from the same address: the device refuses passwords for a while. {seconds} is how many seconds to wait (up to about 60).
